description: Core functionality provided by the VM that isn't related to any kind of I/O.

syscalls.name: memset
syscalls.description: Fill a block of bytes in the heap with a given value.

syscalls.name: memset32
syscalls.description: Fill a region of memory with 32-bit values. This is useful for some graphics operations.

syscalls.name: memcpy
syscalls.description: Copy a block of memory in the heap from a source address to a destination address.

syscalls.name: memcmp
syscalls.description: Compare two sequences of bytes. Returns 0 if equal, -1 if the first mismatching byte has a lower value in `p_a`, 1 if greater.

syscalls.name: vm_heap_size
syscalls.description: Report the current heap size in bytes.

syscalls.name: vm_grow_heap
syscalls.description: Grow the heap to a new size given in bytes. This is similar to the `brk()` system call on POSIX systems. Note that the heap may be resized to a size larger than requested. The heap size is guaranteed to be a multiple of 8 bytes. If the requested size is smaller than the current heap size, this is a no-op. Returns the new heap size in bytes.

syscalls.name: exit
syscalls.description: End program execution with the specified exit status.

syscalls.name: thread_spawn
syscalls.description: Spawn a new thread running the given function with the argument value `arg`.

syscalls.name: thread_id
syscalls.description: Get the id of the current thread.

syscalls.name: thread_sleep
syscalls.description: Make the current thread sleep for at least the given time in milliseconds.

syscalls.name: thread_join
syscalls.description: Join on the thread with the given id. Produces the return value for the thread.

syscalls.name: cmd_argc
syscalls.description: Get the number of command-line arguments passed to the program. Argument 0 is the program file path.

syscalls.name: cmd_get_arg
syscalls.description: Copy command-line argument idx into the buffer dst with capacity dst_len bytes. The copy is NUL-terminated whenever dst_len is at least 1, and truncated to fit. Returns the full byte length of the argument excluding the NUL terminator, so calling with dst_len = 0 queries the size needed.

syscalls.name: print_i64
syscalls.description: Print an i64 value to standard output.

syscalls.name: print_f32
syscalls.description: Print an f32 value to standard output.

syscalls.name: print_str
syscalls.description: Print a string to standard output.

syscalls.name: print_endl
syscalls.description: Print a newline to standard output.

syscalls.name: putchar
syscalls.description: Write one byte to standard output. This is a blocking function. The value -1 is returned on end of file or error. Otherwise the byte written is returned.

syscalls.name: getchar
syscalls.description: Read one byte from standard input. This is a blocking function. The value -1 is returned on end of file or error.

description: Date, time and timing related system calls.

syscalls.name: time_current_ms
syscalls.description: Get the UNIX time stamp in milliseconds.

description: Functionality related to creating windows, drawing graphics, as well as mouse and keyboard input.

syscalls.name: window_create
syscalls.description: Create a new window with a frame buffer to draw into. The window is initially hidden when created, and will appear as soon as the first frame of image data is drawn.

syscalls.name: window_draw_frame
syscalls.description: Copy a frame of pixels to be displayed into the window. The frame must have the same width and height as the window. The pixel format is 32 bits per pixel in BGRA byte order, with 8 bits for each component and the B byte at the lowest address.

syscalls.name: window_poll_event
syscalls.description: Try to read an event from the windowing system if available. The event is read into an event struct. Boolean true is returned if an event was read, false if not.

syscalls.name: window_wait_event
syscalls.description: Block until an window event is available.

syscalls.name: audio_open_output
syscalls.description: Open an audio output device for blocking playback. Returns a device id used with audio_wait_output / audio_write / audio_close. The device runs on the caller's own thread(s): no callback thread is spawned.

syscalls.name: audio_wait_output
syscalls.description: Block until the output device needs the next buffer of samples, then return. Call audio_write next to hand it the samples. This just-in-time rendezvous keeps output latency to about one buffer period.

syscalls.name: audio_write
syscalls.description: Submit num_frames of interleaved samples (num_frames * num_channels i16 values) to the output device, copying them into the device buffer. Intended to follow audio_wait_output.

syscalls.name: audio_open_input
syscalls.description: Open an audio input device for blocking capture. Returns a device id used with audio_read / audio_close. The device runs on the caller's own thread(s): no callback thread is spawned.

syscalls.name: audio_read
syscalls.description: Block until num_frames of interleaved input samples (num_frames * num_channels i16 values) have been captured, then copy them into the provided buffer.

syscalls.name: audio_close
syscalls.description: Close an audio device (input or output), stopping it and unblocking any thread waiting in audio_wait_output / audio_read.

syscalls.name: net_listen
syscalls.description: Open a listening TCP socket bound to the given address (e.g. "127.0.0.1:9000"). Returns a socket id (a positive integer) to be passed to net_accept, or -1 on failure.

syscalls.name: net_accept
syscalls.description: Block until an incoming connection is received on a listening socket, then create a new socket for it. The client's address is written into client_addr_buf as a NUL-terminated string, truncated to addr_buf_len. Returns the new connection's socket id (a positive integer), or -1 if the listening socket is closed (by net_close from another thread) or on error.

syscalls.name: net_read
syscalls.description: Read data from a socket into a buffer with the given capacity. Blocks until at least one byte is available (unless a read timeout has been set with net_set_read_timeout). Returns the number of bytes read, 0 when the connection has been closed by the peer, -1 on error, or -2 if the read timed out.

syscalls.name: net_write
syscalls.description: Write data to an open socket. Blocks until the entire buffer has been written. Returns the number of bytes written, or -1 if the connection was lost.

syscalls.name: net_close
syscalls.description: Close an open socket. Closing a listening socket also cancels a thread blocked in net_accept on it; closing a connected socket wakes a thread blocked in net_read on it. Returns 0 on success, or NET_ERROR if the socket id is unknown.

syscalls.name: net_set_read_timeout
syscalls.description: Set the read timeout on a connected socket, in milliseconds. When set, net_read blocks for at most timeout_ms and returns NET_TIMEOUT if no data arrives in that window. A timeout of 0 clears the timeout, making subsequent reads block indefinitely. Returns 0 on success, or NET_ERROR on failure.

description: File I/O and filesystem-related functionality. This subsystem is separated out from the general-purpose io subsystem for security reasons.

syscalls.name: file_open
syscalls.description: Open the file at the given path. The flags argument is a bitfield combining OPEN_READ, OPEN_WRITE, OPEN_CREATE and OPEN_TRUNC. All access is binary (byte-exact) with no newline translation. Returns a nonzero file handle on success, or 0 on failure (for example if the path is rejected by the sandbox or does not exist).

syscalls.name: file_close
syscalls.description: Close a file handle previously returned by file_open. Has no effect if the handle is not open.

syscalls.name: file_read
syscalls.description: Read up to num_bytes from the file into the buffer. Returns the number of bytes actually read, 0 at end of file, or -1 on error.

syscalls.name: file_write
syscalls.description: Write num_bytes from the buffer to the file. Returns the number of bytes actually written, or -1 on error.

syscalls.name: file_seek
syscalls.description: Seek to an absolute byte offset measured from the start of the file. Returns the new absolute position.

syscalls.name: file_tell
syscalls.description: Return the current absolute byte offset, measured from the start of the file.

syscalls.name: file_size
syscalls.description: Return the total size of the file in bytes. Does not change the current file position.
